root.name: agentfox
root.help: Agent-native, vendor-neutral governance for AI agents in production.

commands.name: init
commands.summary: Set everything up.
commands.help:
Set everything up. Idempotent, offline, and safe to run twice.

Creates the database, applies migrations, loads the control catalog and the
shipped policy packs, each in the mode it declares (baseline and
eu-ai-act-high-risk observe; tool-containment enforces; coding-agent only for
agents this repo's coding-harness hooks govern), and writes a
agentfox.toml carrying the real runtime defaults so they are visible rather than
implicit. AGENTFOX_* environment variables (or the legacy NOMETRIA_* names)
override that file.

params.name: path
params.help: Where to write agentfox.toml. Default: here.

params.name: environment
params.help: Name this deployment: development, staging or production. It decides how strictly `agentfox doctor` grades authentication.

params.name: demo
params.help: Also load the demo fixtures: three agents and an eval suite. No traffic is recorded; run `agentfox demo` afterwards for sample traces and findings.

commands.name: demo
commands.summary: Run the end-to-end walkthrough (offline).
commands.help: Run the end-to-end walkthrough (offline).

commands.name: scan
commands.summary: Find what is worth governing: a repo, local sessions, an MCP server, the runtime.
commands.help:
Find what is worth governing: a repo, local sessions, an MCP server, the runtime.

`agentfox scan [PATH] [--fail] [--json]` scans a repository (the default). `agentfox scan --sessions [PATH]` also reads local AI-tool sessions and runs the live detector check. `mcp`, `skills` and `runtime` scan the rest.

commands.name: skills
commands.summary: Scan agent skills for planted instructions and declared danger.
commands.help:
Scan agent skills for planted instructions and declared danger.

A skill is the same object as an MCP tool one layer up: a description the
model reads to decide whether to invoke it, and instructions it then obeys.
OWASP published an Agentic Skills Top 10 in 2026 and we scanned servers but
not skills.

params.name: path
params.help: Directory to search for SKILL.md files.

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Check an MCP server: what it can reach, how it is pinned, and its tools.
commands.help:
Check an MCP server: what it can reach, how it is pinned, and its tools.

Reads your MCP client config and registers every server it declares, so there is
nothing to set up first. Nothing is started: without --file the check covers
what the config shows (version pinning, remote auth, credentials in the file) and
what the server can reach. With --file (the server's tools/list output) it also
snapshots the tools and flags poisoned descriptions and changes since last time.

params.name: server
params.help: Server name as your MCP config declares it. Omit to scan every one.

params.name: file
params.help: Tool list JSON (what the server's tools/list returned).

params.name: config
params.help: MCP client config to read servers from. Default: the first of .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .claude/settings.json, .claude.json and claude_desktop_config.json found in this directory.

params.name: seed_fixture
params.help: Scan the built-in demo tool list instead of --file. For demos only.

commands.name: repo
commands.summary: Scan a repository and highlight everything worth governing.
commands.help:
Scan a repository and highlight everything worth governing.

Static only: reads the source, never imports or runs it. Importing the target
would execute arbitrary code from a repo the operator may not trust, and would
fail on anything with an import-time side effect — which is most real
applications. Stays entirely local unless `--submit` (or an interactive "yes")
opts into sending a redacted summary — see `cli/submit.py`.

params.name: as_json
params.help: Full records for scripts: every site, whole paths, no table.

params.name: limit
params.help: How many sites to show, worst first.

params.name: fail_on_ungoverned
params.help: Exit non-zero if any model call is ungoverned (for CI).

params.name: submit
params.help: Send a redacted summary (counts and structure only, never file contents) to a running control plane for a fuller dashboard report. Optional — omit both flags to be asked interactively.

commands.name: runtime
commands.summary: Sweep for shadow agents, unowned agents, registry drift, identity posture and delegation cycles/depth.
commands.help:
Sweep for shadow agents, unowned agents, registry drift, identity posture and
delegation cycles/depth.

commands.name: agents
commands.summary: Find every agent that is running, and who owns it.
commands.help: Find every agent that is running, and who owns it.

commands.name: list
commands.summary: List every agent, registered or shadow.
commands.help: List every agent, registered or shadow.

params.name: stopped
params.help: Only agents that are quarantined or killed, and why.

commands.name: register
commands.summary: Register an agent (or update one), so it is owned rather than shadow.
commands.help:
Register an agent (or update one), so it is owned rather than shadow.

Agents also appear on their first call; registering one up front gives it an
owner and an environment before it has run, and turns a shadow agent into a
registered one. Options left out keep the agent's current values.

params.name: owner
params.help: Owner's email. An agent with no owner is a finding.

params.name: env
params.help: Environment it runs in. Default: production, or its current one.

params.name: risk_tier
params.help: minimal | limited | high | prohibited. Default: limited, or its current one.

commands.name: budget
commands.summary: Show or set an agent's budget: the caps `budget.exceeded` blocks on.
commands.help:
Show or set an agent's budget: the caps `budget.exceeded` blocks on.

With no option it prints the current caps and usage. Each option sets one cap and
leaves the others as they are; 0 removes that cap. Over a cap, the agent's calls
are blocked (`budget.exhausted`) until the window rolls over.

params.name: max_depth
params.help: Longest tool-call chain in one run.

commands.name: lineage
commands.summary: Show what an agent reaches — the blast radius.
commands.help: Show what an agent reaches — the blast radius.

commands.name: quarantine
commands.summary: Stop an agent while you investigate.
commands.help: Stop an agent while you investigate. Reversible and audited.

commands.name: kill
commands.summary: Stop an agent now.
commands.help: Stop an agent now.

commands.name: resume
commands.summary: Restart a stopped agent.
commands.help: Restart a stopped agent.

commands.name: serve
commands.summary: Run the gateway and control-plane API, or the MCP server for AI clients.
commands.help:
Run the gateway and control-plane API, or the MCP server for AI clients.

`agentfox serve [--host] [--port] [--reload]` starts the API (the default); `agentfox serve mcp` speaks MCP over stdio.

commands.name: api
commands.summary: Start the gateway and control-plane API.
commands.help: Start the gateway and control-plane API.

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Serve MCP over stdio (for Claude Code, Claude Desktop and other MCP clients).
commands.help:
Serve MCP over stdio (for Claude Code, Claude Desktop and other MCP clients).

Read-only by design: nothing that changes enforcement or stops an agent is exposed.

commands.name: findings
commands.summary: What the platform found.
commands.help:
What the platform found. The list `agentfox.auto()` tells you to read.

Ordered worst first, then most recently seen. A finding that keeps happening is
one row with a count, not one row per occurrence, so the length of this list is
the number of distinct problems.

params.name: severity
params.help: Show only this severity: critical, high, medium, low or info.

params.name: limit
params.help: How many findings to show, worst first.

params.name: as_json
params.help: Full records for scripts: whole ids, fingerprints, subjects and timestamps.

commands.name: permit
commands.summary: Grant, list and withdraw what an agent — or an end user — may do, and decide the calls held for a person (`permit approvals`).
commands.help: Grant, list and withdraw what an agent — or an end user — may do, and decide the calls held for a person (`permit approvals`).

commands.name: grant
commands.summary: Allow an agent to call a tool, and say under what limits.
commands.help:
Allow an agent to call a tool, and say under what limits.

Least privilege is default deny: an agent with no grant for a tool cannot call
it, whether or not a detector fires. This command is the only thing that widens
that, so it asks before it writes and records the result in the audit chain.

params.name: tool
params.help: Tool key this grant covers. A glob is allowed: tickets.* or *.

params.name: action
params.help: Action on the tool this grant covers, repeatable. Default: every action.

params.name: limit
params.help: Argument limit, repeatable. path=value, or path:op=value — for example --limit amount:lt=1000 --limit currency:in=USD,EUR.

params.name: max_taint
params.help: Worst provenance an argument may carry and still go through without an approval. One of: none, user, retrieved, tool_result, subagent, memory.

params.name: requires_approval
params.help: Send every matching call to a human before it runs.

params.name: expires_in_days
params.help: Withdraw the grant automatically after this many days. Default: no expiry.

params.name: granted_by
params.help: Who is accountable for this grant. Recorded in the audit.

params.name: yes
params.help: Skip the confirmation prompt (for scripts and CI).

commands.name: list
commands.summary: What each agent is allowed to do.
commands.help: What each agent is allowed to do. Anything not listed here is refused.

params.name: agent
params.help: Agent slug. Omit to list every agent's grants.

commands.name: revoke
commands.summary: Withdraw a grant.
commands.help: Withdraw a grant. The agent's calls to that tool are refused from now on.

params.name: capability_id
params.help: Grant id from `agentfox permit list`, e.g. cap_01h....

params.name: yes
params.help: Skip the confirmation prompt (for scripts and CI).

commands.name: user
commands.summary: Grant access to a resource pattern.
commands.help: Grant access to a resource pattern.

params.name: principal
params.help: Group or subject the grant is for.

commands.name: approvals
commands.summary: See the calls waiting for a person, and approve or deny them.
commands.help: See the calls waiting for a person, and approve or deny them.

commands.name: list
commands.summary: The calls held for a person.
commands.help: The calls held for a person. Unanswered ones expire, and expiry denies.

params.name: status
params.help: pending (the default), approved, denied, expired, used, or all.

commands.name: show
commands.summary: One approval in full: the call, its arguments, why it was held, and the decision.
commands.help: One approval in full: the call, its arguments, why it was held, and the decision.

params.name: approval_id
params.help: Approval id, or the short id `list` prints.

commands.name: approve
commands.summary: Let the held call run once: the same agent, tool and arguments, when retried.
commands.help: Let the held call run once: the same agent, tool and arguments, when retried.

params.name: approval_id
params.help: Approval id, or the short id `list` prints.

params.name: actor
params.help: Who is deciding (an email), for the audit record.

commands.name: deny
commands.summary: Refuse the held call.
commands.help: Refuse the held call. A retry presenting this approval escalates again.

params.name: approval_id
params.help: Approval id, or the short id `list` prints.

params.name: actor
params.help: Who is deciding (an email), for the audit record.

commands.name: declare
commands.summary: Declare the facts containment reasons over: tools, data scope, sources, hand-offs.
commands.help:
Declare the facts containment reasons over: tools, data scope, sources, hand-offs.

What a tool can do, which column says whose row it is, what an agent has no data for, which sources are authoritative, and when to hand off to a person.

commands.name: tool
commands.summary: Declare a tool and what it can do.
commands.help:
Declare a tool and what it can do.

Containment is declared, not detected: an irreversible tool recorded as `read` is one
a tainted argument can reach. This is the command that makes least privilege real, and
it is deliberately the first thing `agentfox init` points at.

params.name: impact
params.help: read | write | high_impact | irreversible — the axis every containment rule reasons over.

params.name: output_trust
params.help: untrusted | trusted — whether values copied out of this tool's output taint the arguments they land in. Default for a new tool: untrusted. Declare trusted only for a system of record you control, such as a CRM read.

commands.name: triggers
commands.summary: declare what a tool call sets off downstream (a DB trigger, a webhook, a fan-out), so `cascade_risk()` can actually see it.
commands.help:
declare what a tool call sets off downstream (a DB trigger, a webhook, a
fan-out), so `cascade_risk()` can actually see it. An undeclared trigger stays
invisible by design (see `effects.cascade_risk`'s own docstring) — this is how
an operator closes that gap for one tool.

params.name: triggers
params.help: Comma-separated tool keys this call sets off downstream

commands.name: scope
commands.summary: declare which column on a table decides whose row it is, so `analyse_access()` can prove a query is scoped instead of assuming it.
commands.help:
declare which column on a table decides whose row it is, so
`analyse_access()` can prove a query is scoped instead of assuming it. An
undeclared table is reported, never assumed safe (see `data_access`'s own
docstring).

params.name: column
params.help: Column that decides whose row it is

params.name: principal_key
params.help: Attribute of the calling principal the column must equal

params.name: restricted_columns
params.help: Comma-separated columns nobody should receive even for their own row

commands.name: reference
commands.summary: declare a table that belongs to nobody, so `analyse_access()` does not flag it as an undeclared/unscoped table.
commands.help:
declare a table that belongs to nobody, so `analyse_access()` does not
flag it as an undeclared/unscoped table.

params.name: table
params.help: Table name — belongs to nobody (currencies, statuses, postcodes)

commands.name: boundary
commands.summary: Declare what an agent is allowed to answer from.
commands.help:
Declare what an agent is allowed to answer from.

Until this exists nothing stops the agent inventing an answer to a question it has
no data for, which is the single failure most likely to reach a customer.

Re-running it changes only the options you pass, so `--mode enforce` on its own
switches enforcement on and keeps the systems, coverage and topics already declared.

params.name: answerable
params.help: Question types this agent may answer (default fact,aggregate,procedure).

params.name: mode
params.help: observe | enforce (a new boundary starts in observe)

commands.name: source
commands.summary: Register a source and its authority tier.
commands.help: Register a source and its authority tier.

params.name: updated
params.help: When the source last changed (ISO, or 'now').

commands.name: import-sources
commands.summary: Bulk-register from a JSON file.
commands.help:
Bulk-register from a JSON file.

Tiering a corpus is inherently a bulk act. Nobody classifies four hundred sources
one command at a time, and making them try is how the tiering never happens.

commands.name: escalation
commands.summary: Declare when this agent must hand off to a human.
commands.help: Declare when this agent must hand off to a human.

params.name: agent
params.help: Agent slug; omit for the default.

params.name: mode
params.help: observe: record missed escalations as findings. enforce: hand the conversation off on the turn it qualifies.

commands.name: principal
commands.summary: Register the human an agent acts for.
commands.help:
Register the human an agent acts for.

Everything else in this pillar depends on this. The Copilot failure is its absence:
the agent runs under its own identity, inherits everything that identity can reach,
and every permission check passes.

params.name: subject
params.help: IdP subject — an OIDC `sub` or employee id.

commands.name: list
commands.summary: Everything declared so far: tools and their impact, sources and their tier.
commands.help: Everything declared so far: tools and their impact, sources and their tier.

params.name: kind
params.help: tools, sources, or all (the default; not with --json).

commands.name: policy
commands.summary: Write the rules, try them against recorded traffic, then turn them on.
commands.help: Write the rules, try them against recorded traffic, then turn them on.

commands.name: packs
commands.summary: Policy packs on disk, and where each came from.
commands.help:
Policy packs on disk, and where each came from.

`policy list` reads the database: what is installed and what mode it is in.
This reads the filesystem and answers the question an operator has about a
policy they did not write — which file is this, and did something override
it. A project pack replacing a shipped one is invisible in `policy list`,
because by then they are the same row.

commands.name: list
commands.summary: List policies and their enforcement mode.
commands.help: List policies and their enforcement mode.

commands.name: lint
commands.summary: Lint the policy hierarchy, or policy files.
commands.help:
Lint the policy hierarchy, or policy files. Exits 1 on critical or high findings.

This is the half of hierarchical policy that produces the 87% misconfiguration
reduction — composition without a linter just moves the confusion somewhere
harder to see. Pass files to check them before they are loaded, e.g. in CI.

params.name: files
params.help: Policy files to lint, as org-level layers in the order given. Without files, lints every bound policy layer.

commands.name: effective
commands.summary: Show the policy actually in force for a subject, and where each rule came from.
commands.help:
Show the policy actually in force for a subject, and where each rule came from.

Opacity is what makes layered policy dangerous, so the resolver explains itself.

params.name: environment
params.help: Environment to resolve for. Defaults to the configured environment (NOMETRIA_ENVIRONMENT), which is what the runtime itself uses.

commands.name: simulate
commands.summary: Replay recorded traffic against a candidate policy.
commands.help:
Replay recorded traffic against a candidate policy.

Exits non-zero when the change would newly block production traffic, so it can
gate a policy PR the same way `eval gate` gates a code PR.

commands.name: enforce
commands.summary: Promote a policy from observe to enforce.
commands.help: Promote a policy from observe to enforce.

commands.name: observe
commands.summary: Demote a policy from enforce to observe.
commands.help: Demote a policy from enforce to observe.

commands.name: validate
commands.summary: Check, lint and compile a policy file without saving it.
commands.help:
Check, lint and compile a policy file without saving it.

Runs the full lint (`policy lint FILE`), so a rule that can never fire or a
condition naming an unknown value (`surface: [toolargs]`) fails validation.
Exits 1 on a parse error or a critical/high finding.

commands.name: catalogue
commands.summary: Every kind of guardrail this product can enforce.
commands.help:
Every kind of guardrail this product can enforce.

The answer to "can we express our policy?" — asked before anyone writes YAML.

commands.name: compile
commands.summary: Turn a written policy into executable guardrails.
commands.help: Turn a written policy into executable guardrails.

commands.name: rules
commands.summary: Business rules in plain terms: apply, show, check, explain, suggest, graph.
commands.help: Business rules in plain terms: apply, show, check, explain, suggest, graph.

commands.name: apply
commands.summary: Author or update a business rule from a YAML file.
commands.help: Author or update a business rule from a YAML file.

commands.name: show
commands.summary: Show the resolved bands, so an author sees exactly what they wrote.
commands.help: Show the resolved bands, so an author sees exactly what they wrote.

commands.name: check
commands.summary: Find where two teams' rules disagree.
commands.help:
Find where two teams' rules disagree.

Two authors setting different thresholds on the same field is not a merge to be
resolved by precedence — it is a disagreement between two people, and resolving it
silently means one of them is wrong and does not know.

commands.name: test
commands.summary: Try values against a rule without running anything.
commands.help: Try values against a rule without running anything.

commands.name: catalogue
commands.summary: Every kind of guardrail this product can enforce.
commands.help:
Every kind of guardrail this product can enforce.

The answer to "can we express our policy?" — asked before anyone writes YAML.

commands.name: explain
commands.summary: Parameters, inputs and a worked example for one guardrail kind.
commands.help: Parameters, inputs and a worked example for one guardrail kind.

commands.name: suggest
commands.summary: Which guardrail kinds a written instruction probably needs.
commands.help:
Which guardrail kinds a written instruction probably needs.

Deterministic signal matching, not a model — a starting point an operator confirms,
so a wrong suggestion costs a glance rather than a silent misconfiguration.

params.name: instruction
params.help: A sentence from a policy document.

commands.name: graph
commands.summary: The decision path as it will actually run, stage by stage.
commands.help: The decision path as it will actually run, stage by stage.

commands.name: compile
commands.summary: Turn a written policy into executable guardrails.
commands.help: Turn a written policy into executable guardrails.

commands.name: proposals
commands.summary: Proposed changes to governance configuration: review, decide, apply, undo.
commands.help: Proposed changes to governance configuration: review, decide, apply, undo.

commands.name: list
commands.summary: List proposals, newest first.
commands.help: List proposals, newest first.

commands.name: show
commands.summary: Show one proposal: its diff, evidence, proof and decisions.
commands.help: Show one proposal: its diff, evidence, proof and decisions.

commands.name: approve
commands.summary: Approve a proven proposal.
commands.help: Approve a proven proposal. An org-level loosening needs two different people.

params.name: actor
params.help: Your name or email — decisions are named

commands.name: reject
commands.summary: Reject a proposal.
commands.help: Reject a proposal.

params.name: actor
params.help: Your name or email — decisions are named

commands.name: apply
commands.summary: Apply an approved proposal (or settle one whose canary has finished).
commands.help: Apply an approved proposal (or settle one whose canary has finished).

params.name: automated
params.help: Apply as the improvement loop, subject to autonomy, freeze and daily cap

commands.name: rollback
commands.summary: Undo an applied or canaried proposal.
commands.help: Undo an applied or canaried proposal.

commands.name: verify
commands.summary: Close the loop on an applied change: did it do what it promised?
commands.help:
Close the loop on an applied change: did it do what it promised?

`--failed` rolls the change back. If undoing it would loosen a control, it stays
applied with the failure recorded, because that rollback is a person's decision.

params.name: failed
params.help: The change did not do what it promised: record it and roll back.

commands.name: from-labels
commands.summary: File rule cut-off proposals from labelled false positives.
commands.help: File rule cut-off proposals from labelled false positives. Nothing is applied.

commands.name: from-traffic
commands.summary: Propose tool declarations and grants from what your agents have called.
commands.help:
Propose tool declarations and grants from what your agents have called.

Learned permissions: observe, propose, approve. Reads every recorded tool call —
refused ones included — and files a `tool.declare` for each undeclared tool and a
`capability.grant` per agent and tool, with argument limits read off the calls and
a provenance ceiling from benign calls only. A call a detector matched, or that was
stopped for where its arguments came from and nobody approved, is never learned
from. Nothing is applied: approve and apply each proposal.

params.name: since
params.help: Window: 7d, 24h, 30m or an ISO date. Default: the last 30 days.

commands.name: test
commands.summary: Prove the controls hold before you ship: score, gate, attack, and dry-run.
commands.help: Prove the controls hold before you ship: score, gate, attack, and dry-run.

commands.name: run
commands.summary: Run an evaluation suite.
commands.help: Run an evaluation suite.

commands.name: gate
commands.summary: Run the suite and fail the build on regression or on any errored case.
commands.help: Run the suite and fail the build on regression or on any errored case. Exits 1 on failure.

params.name: agent
params.help: Agent to fit the envelope for. Default: the baseline run's agent.

params.name: scorers
params.help: Comma-separated scorer keys. Default: the baseline run's scorers.

commands.name: baseline
commands.summary: Mark a run as the regression baseline.
commands.help: Mark a run as the regression baseline.

commands.name: suites
commands.summary: List the evaluation suites in this deployment.
commands.help: List the evaluation suites in this deployment.

commands.name: online
commands.summary: Sample production traffic and score it with the offline scorers.
commands.help: Sample production traffic and score it with the offline scorers.

commands.name: redteam
commands.summary: Run adversarial probes against the deployed configuration.
commands.help:
Run adversarial probes against the deployed configuration.

This measures whether *this configuration* got weaker, against known attack classes.
It is not a robustness certificate, and `--adaptive` does not make it one: every
published result says an attacker who adapts eventually gets through.

Exits 1 when any attack got through (unless --allow-escapes). Probes are simulated:
their tool calls are evaluated without writing decisions, so they never show up
in findings or in what `policy simulate` replays. The campaign itself, and a
finding naming the attacks that got through, are recorded.

params.name: adaptive
params.help: Mutate a blocked probe and try again, steering from the failure. Reports a posture delta against the last comparable campaign, not a pass rate.

params.name: budget
params.help: Attempts per probe in adaptive mode.

params.name: deployment_probes
params.help: Adaptive mode only: also generate probes from this deployment's own grants, impacts and bound policies (on by default with --adaptive). The static suite always runs the built-in probes alone.

params.name: allow_escapes
params.help: Exit 0 even when an attack got through. By default an escaped attack exits 1, so the command can gate CI.

commands.name: probes
commands.summary: List the built-in probe suite and available wrapped runners.
commands.help: List the built-in probe suite and available wrapped runners.

commands.name: action
commands.summary: Read an artefact and say what running it would actually do.
commands.help:
Read an artefact and say what running it would actually do.

Deterministic, offline and immediate: no database, no model, no network. The point
is that an engineer can check a generated statement before it is ever executed.

params.name: statement
params.help: SQL, shell command or URL to analyse

commands.name: boundary
commands.summary: Would this question be refused, and what would we say instead?
commands.help:
Would this question be refused, and what would we say instead?

Changes nothing, so it is safe to replay real traffic through before enforcing —
which matters more here than anywhere else, because the false positives of this
control are refusals shown to customers.

commands.name: rule
commands.summary: Try values against a rule without running anything.

What you can show an auditor: posture, evidence, risk, sign-off.

params.name: agent
params.help: Only this agent. Repeat for several. Default: all.

commands.help: Build an auditor-ready evidence package.

params.name: to

commands.help: Show the agent risk register.

commands.name: obligations
commands.summary: Regulatory obligation calendar against the agent inventory.
commands.help: Regulatory obligation calendar against the agent inventory.

commands.name: frameworks
commands.summary: List frameworks, coverage and review status.
commands.help: List frameworks, coverage and review status.

commands.summary: Executive risk view.

commands.name: review-packet
commands.summary: Everything a qualified reviewer needs to sign off one framework, in one file.
commands.help:
Everything a qualified reviewer needs to sign off one framework, in one file.

Every mapping ships `DRAFT — UNVERIFIED / NOT LEGAL ADVICE` until a named human reviews
it, and that is the loudest "not ready" signal in an audit conversation. The blocker has
never been the workflow, it has been that nobody could hand a reviewer a reviewable
artefact. This is that artefact: the control, what implements it, what evidence it
produces, and the exact clause claimed — one row per decision the reviewer has to make.

params.name: out
params.help: Write markdown here instead of stdout.

commands.name: signoff
commands.summary: Record a qualified reviewer's sign-off on a control's framework mapping(s).
commands.help:
Record a qualified reviewer's sign-off on a control's framework mapping(s).

This is an attestation by a named person, recorded and auditable. It is the step that
moves a mapping from `DRAFT — UNVERIFIED / NOT LEGAL ADVICE` to reviewed, and it should
be run by whoever is actually accountable for the claim — not by whoever runs the CLI.

params.name: reviewer
params.help: The human accountable for this sign-off.

params.name: reference
params.help: Sign off one clause only; default is every clause for the control.

commands.name: entitlement
commands.summary: How much more the agent can reach than its callers are entitled to.
commands.help:

Worth running before any entitlement model exists — a ratio of 1.0 with no grants
configured is exactly the point.

commands.name: escalations
commands.summary: Which conversations qualified for a human and never got one.
commands.help:
Which conversations qualified for a human and never got one.

The largest single failure family at 31%, and invisible from inside the system: a
conversation where the agent kept going instead of handing off looks entirely
ordinary in the telemetry.

commands.help:

each one names the consequence rather than the setting, because "fail_mode=open"
means nothing to someone who has not read the PRD.

commands.name: hooks
commands.summary: Run AgentFox where the agent already is: a warm daemon and a thin per-call hook.
commands.help: Run AgentFox where the agent already is: a warm daemon and a thin per-call hook.

commands.name: daemon
commands.summary: Run the warm process a hook talks to.
commands.help:
Run the warm process a hook talks to.

A harness spawns its hook as a fresh process per tool call, and importing
AgentFox costs seconds — measured here at 3.9s on the first call against a
cold daemon, then 6ms once warm. That gap is the whole reason this exists:
a hook that costs two seconds a call is a hook the operator removes.

commands.name: run
commands.summary: The per-call hook.
commands.help:
The per-call hook. Reads the harness payload on stdin, writes its reply.

Everything in this path runs in a process the harness creates and destroys
per tool call, so it does the least possible: parse, ask the daemon, print.
Measured against a warm daemon, the round trip is about 6ms; the same work
without one is 3.9 seconds, because `import agentfox` is.

params.name: agent
params.help: Agent slug to govern this session as.

commands.name: install
commands.summary: Show, or write, the hook configuration for a harness.
commands.help:
Show, or write, the hook configuration for a harness.

Dry by default. This edits a file that decides whether the operator's agent
runs at all, so it prints what it would do and waits to be told twice.

With --write it also sets up a working baseline: the agent is registered
(development unless --env says otherwise), the harness's built-in tools are
declared with their real impact and granted to it, and the coding-agent pack is
bound to it in observe. Destructive commands are still refused.

params.name: agent
params.help: Agent slug these calls are governed as.

params.name: environment
params.help: Environment the agent runs in. Default: development for a new agent; an agent already registered keeps its own.

params.name: grant
params.help: Grant the harness's built-in tools to the agent (the default), so ordinary work is not refused by default-deny.
